current.text: He opted into a 1-year, 49 million USD contract after he could not find a new team. This is the final year of his deal, and the Kings have no interest in extending him.
Schroder, Westbrook and DeRozan have left Sacramento. He now shares the ball mainly with Sabonis.
Experts expect more usage and more ball handling for him, and a bigger part in the offense.
His assists could rise a lot. Better-shooting teammates and better luck should help him convert more potential assists.
He is a projected starter next to Acuff, Hunter, Murray and Sabonis. Coach Ham calls him the Kings' second best player behind Sabonis.
One expert expects him to start and play 30 or more minutes.
His role is unclear. The rebuilding Kings could trade him, buy him out, bench him or cut his minutes, and that risk drags his draft value down.

Experts see him as good value at his market price. Without the Kings risk he would rank two tiers higher. He should easily beat his ranking per game, could be a top-80 player, and is a top-50 player when he is firing.

Experts expect Sacramento near the bottom of the league, but they disagree on how the team will act. Lloyd expects the Kings to trade or sit veterans. Others expect the team to keep trying to win games to stay out of the relegation zone.
Coach Doug Christie is under the most pressure and may lean on veterans to win games.

durable.text: He is an efficient shooter. He has elite free throw shooting, an elite field goal percentage for his position and a good three-point percentage.

note: He costs almost nothing on the market (1.2 USD average cost on both sites, Yahoo value 5 USD, ESPN rank 159), but our league paid 12 USD for him last season. He goes around picks 107 to 114 in 9-cat mocks, and experts see top-80 upside if he keeps his starter role. At 1 to 5 USD he is a cheap source of 3PM, PTS and FT% with a good FG% for a guard, so he fits builds that can live with weak steals, blocks and rebounds. Early in the season, check that he still starts with 30 or more minutes and more usage, and watch for trade, buyout or benching news from Sacramento.
